Approving. I verified the claims against the code rather than the description, with an independent cross-vendor review as a second pass, and both hold up. One note on framing first, because I think this PR undersells itself.

## This is a data-loss fix, not just an output fix

On current `main`, the single-issue delete path gates the preview on `if !force` (`cmd/bd/delete.go:136`) and the destructive branch below it never consults `dryRun`. So `bd delete <id> --force --dry-run` **actually deletes the issue** — `--dry-run` is silently ignored whenever `--force` is present. That is exactly the shape a user reaches for when they want to check a forced delete before committing to it. The PR's `if dryRun || !force` gate closes it. Worth saying out loud in the title/description, since "preserve forced delete dry-runs" reads as cosmetic.

## What I verified

- **`--force` reaches single and batch dry-run previews without mutating.** Single forwards `force` with `dryRun=true`; batch now passes `force` through to `DeleteIssues` instead of the hardcoded `false`. In `issueops/delete.go`, `force` only widens dependent discovery, and the `dryRun` return happens before any delete, dependency removal, reference rewrite, or blocked-state recomputation. Embedded Dolt opens the dry-run transaction non-committing; server Dolt suppresses wisp deletion and returns before staging/commit; the proxied domain path returns before all writes and closes through rollback.
- **Quiet previews are empty, JSON previews are structural-only.** The JSON preview carries IDs, mode flags, counts and orphan count — no titles or descriptions — and JSON correctly takes precedence over quiet. I checked the error path specifically: `outputDeletionPreview` writes the preview to stdout and `outputJSONError` writes to stderr, so the two calls in sequence do not produce two JSON documents on one stream.
- **No change to the destructive path.** The only incidental behavioural change is that proxied JSON encoding failures are now returned rather than discarded, which is an improvement.

## Two low-severity notes (non-blocking)

1. `TestOutputDeleteProxiedPreviewIsPayloadBlind` constructs a `deleteInput` and a synthetic result and calls only the output helper, so it bypasses flag gathering, `runDeleteProxiedPreviewTx`, and UOW rollback. Its name also falls outside the `TestProxiedServer*` selector in `.github/scripts/proxied-test-shard.sh`, so it will not run in the PR-risk proxied lane. The proxied quiet/privacy boundary is correct by inspection but is not regression-gated on PRs. Renaming it into the `TestProxiedServer*` namespace would be a cheap improvement — happy to do that maintainer-side rather than asking you for another round trip.
2. The proxied-server preview passes `Cascade:true, DryRun:true` but no `Force`. That is consistent with that backend's always-cascade policy, where `--force` is a confirmation gate rather than orphaning semantics — but it does mean there is no force-parity across backends, so the description shouldn't be read as claiming one.

Also noted (pre-existing, not yours to fix here): the embedded and proxied JSON preview schemas diverge — `issue_ids`/`would_remove_*`/`would_orphan` versus `ids`/`*_removed`/`connected`.

On the release request in the description: release cutting is a separate maintainer decision tracked on its own issues, so it will not be handled through this PR — but the fix itself is exactly the kind of thing that motivates a cut. Thanks for a tightly scoped patch with real regression coverage.

input.content:
Thanks for this, and apologies for the silence — this sat unanswered on our side, which is a queue-rhythm failure, not a comment on the work. The feature is one we want: closing #4307 by making a synced GitHub issue carry its bead identity and edges is the right shape, and the plumbing fits existing patterns (the push hook, the create-path double-render guard, `tracker.go` sending `fields["body"]` so the hook's output isn't re-rendered).

I ran two independent reviews on different model families before writing this, because the change turns on a round-trip invariant and those are easy to get subtly wrong. Both reviews independently landed on the same two blockers, so I'm confident they're real rather than reviewer noise. One of them fetched `refs/pull/5065/head` and ran an actual probe; the transcripts below are measured, not hypothesized.

## Two blockers

**1. Strip is not the exact inverse of render, so an unpaired start marker deletes user text.**

`StripGitHubSyncBlock` (`internal/github/mapping.go:333`) removes from the *first* start marker to the first end marker, while `RenderGitHubIssueBody` (`:202`) always appends a fresh block at the *end*. If a body contains a start marker with no matching end, the next cycle spans that stray marker across everything between it and the generated block's end marker, and deletes it. Measured against your branch:

```
pull1 local = "base\n\n<!-- ...start -->\n## Beads\nSource: `bd-1`\n\nMY IMPORTANT NOTE"
push  body  = ... two start markers, one end ...
pull2 local = "base"          <- MY IMPORTANT NOTE permanently gone
```

This is reachable without anything adversarial: HTML comments are invisible in rendered Markdown, so someone tidying the visible `## Beads` section in the web editor can delete the closing comment without seeing it. The same mechanism fires on a bead whose description *legitimately* contains a well-formed block — a bead documenting this feature, or a support ticket quoting a synced body. `RenderGitHubIssueBody:206` strips it from the base before appending, the remote loses it, and the next pull writes the stripped version back over the local description.

A related case: dependency titles are interpolated verbatim (`:240-258`), so a dependency titled `x <!-- bd-github-sync: end --> y` terminates the strip early and leaks the remainder into the local description, growing the body on every round trip.

The fix that closes all three at once: anchor the strip to a single **well-formed, trailing** block with line-anchored markers (render only ever emits one, at the end), have `RenderGitHubIssueBody` refuse to append over an unpaired start, and escape or reject markers in interpolated titles.

**2. `ExtractBDIDFromGitHubSyncBlock` reads outside the block, so a GitHub issue can bind to the wrong bead.**

Despite the name, `mapping.go:351` searches the whole body for the first `<!-- bd:`, with no block requirement and no `sync=github-v1` requirement. Probe result on a body where user text mentions a marker before the real one:

```
extracted = "bd-victim"   (want "bd-real")
```

That value flows through `mapping.go:123` to `conv.Issue.ID`, and `internal/tracker/engine.go:434-437` then resolves `existing = localByID[localID]`. The unrelated local bead is updated with this issue's title, description, status and labels, **and has its `external_ref` repointed** to the imposter issue. The realistic trigger is mundane: a contributor copy-pastes a synced issue body into a new issue. On the create path, `GenerateID` only fills an empty ID (`cmd/bd/github.go:493`), so an arbitrary marker string can become a new bead's primary key with a foreign prefix and no validation.

Worth calling out that this makes pull change *issue identity matching*, which is the most consequential behaviour change in the PR and isn't mentioned in the description or in a code comment.

Fix: extract only from inside a paired block, require the `sync=github-v1` token, validate the ID against the local prefix, and refuse to adopt a local bead by ID when it already carries a different `external_ref`.

## Should-fix, not blocking

- **Dependency-query errors are swallowed** (`cmd/bd/github.go`, `if depErr != nil { dependencies = nil }`). A transient storage error pushes a block with the dependency sections silently *deleted*. The GitLab path warns on stderr (`cmd/bd/gitlab.go:733-736`); at minimum match that, better to skip the re-render and leave the previous body intact.
- **Push-dirtiness doesn't consider the rendered body.** The hook supplies `FormatDescription` but no `ContentEqual`, and the engine skips updates on timestamps. So adding or removing a dependency doesn't advance the issue timestamp and the changed tasklist may never reach GitHub; and if dependency B gets its external ref after A was rendered, A can stay permanently linked as `` `bd-B` `` rather than `#N`.
- **`strings.TrimSpace` on both sides** means `Strip(Render(D)) == TrimSpace(D)`, not `D`. Pull normalizes marker-free bodies byte-for-byte — `"    code\r\n"` becomes `"code"`, which changes Markdown semantics for indented code.
- **The rendered lines are probably not GitHub tasklists.** `- [ ] #12 — blocking issue (`bd-blocker`, blocked by)` — GitHub only creates a tracked relationship when the item is a bare issue reference, so the trailing text makes these plain checkboxes. Closed dependencies also render `- [ ]`, so every synced issue gains a permanently-incomplete "0 of N tasks" badge, and a user who ticks a box has it reverted on the next push with no "generated, do not edit" notice.
- **`REDACTED`** asserts that a bare `<!-- bd: ... -->` outside any block must parse. I grepped for `<!-- bd:` and `bd-github-sync` across the tree and found no prior convention — there is no legacy format to be compatible with, and this test is what pins the over-lenient parser behind blocker 2. It should go unless you can point at a real one.
- **Tests don't cover round-trip.** They assert that render output *contains* expected strings and that one canonical block strips cleanly; there's no `render → strip → compare` assertion and none of the adversarial cases. Double-push idempotency and interior CRLF do hold in practice (verified), but nothing pins them. The invariants worth asserting are `Strip(Render(D)) == D` and `Render(Strip(Render(D))) == Render(D)`, across unpaired/nested/truncated markers, markers in user text, hostile dependency titles, CRLF, leading whitespace, and empty descriptions.

## Coordination note

This collides with #4329 (push dedup), which you mention but the two aren't reconciled. That PR's `PushFieldsEqual` compares `local.Description != remote.Body` and `PushContentHash` hashes `local.Description`. After this PR, local descriptions are stripped and remote bodies carry the block, so the comparison is permanently false and the stored hash never matches what was pushed — the dedup is defeated and every sync re-PATCHes every issue. Whichever lands second needs to compare `RenderGitHubIssueBody(...)` output, the way Linear does at `internal/linear/mapping.go:587` with `BuildLinearDescription`. I'll cross-note this on #4329.

Also a release note we should write rather than something for you to fix: the first sync after this lands rewrites every previously-synced issue body, which is one-time notification churn for existing users. Pull on pre-block issues is safe (no marker, empty ID, normal path).

## Where I'd like to take this

The two blockers are surgical — anchored trailing-block framing plus a scoped extractor — and I'd rather not spend a review round trip on them. **My offer: I'll implement blockers 1 and 2 plus the round-trip test table maintainer-side, on top of your commits with your authorship preserved**, and open the result crediting you as the author of the feature. The tasklist-syntax question (item 7) becomes a follow-up issue rather than a gate.

If you'd rather do it yourself, that's genuinely welcome too — say so and I'll leave it with you and review promptly this time. Either way the design here is sound and the feature is going in; only tell me which path you prefer.

#5065 renders a managed block into the GitHub issue body — bead ID marker plus dependency/dependent lines — and strips that block back out on pull, so local bead descriptions stay clean. That interacts directly with the dedup here:

No action needed from you right now — #5065 is not merge-ready (it has two round-trip blockers I've asked about there), so this PR is likely to land first. FILES: cmd/bd/dep.go, cmd/bd/dep_test.go, internal/storage/dolt/dependencies.go, internal/storage/issueops/dependencies.go

BODY:
## Summary

`GetDependenciesWithMetadata` and `GetDependentsWithMetadata` previously silently dropped dependency rows whose target/source issue did not exist in the local Dolt database. In multi-rig (gastown) deployments this hid all cross-rig dep edges from `bd dep list` and any caller that uses these methods (incl. `gt convoy stage` wave computation), producing wrong wave layering and silently-broken epic/parent-child status propagation.

## Repro (before fix)

```sh
cd ~/gt/<rig>
bd create -t task --title "Local issue"        # → gt-foo
bd dep add gt-foo hq-bar                        # add cross-rig dep (target lives in town)
bd dep list gt-foo                              # → "gt-foo has no dependencies" ❌
```

Direct SQL confirms the row exists:
```sql
USE <rig>; SELECT * FROM dependencies WHERE issue_id='gt-foo';
-- gt-foo | hq-bar | blocks   (row IS there)
```

## Fix

In both `DoltStore.GetDependenciesWithMetadata` and the shared `issueops.GetDependenciesWithMetadataInTx` / `GetDependentsWithMetadataInTx`, emit a placeholder `IssueWithDependencyMetadata` (Issue with only `ID` populated) when the target/source is not local, instead of `continue`-ing past the row.

`bd dep list` now renders cross-rig placeholders as:
```
  hq-bar: (cross-rig) via blocks

## Why

`doctor --fix` can issue its DELETEs against a different database than the one `doctor` diagnosed.

The read-only checks go through `SharedStore`, which opens one already-verified `dolt.DoltStore`. But every destructive fix entry point instead calls `openFixDB`/`openDoltDB` in `cmd/bd/doctor/fix/remotes.go`, which dials a **fresh** connection and re-derives the port from `doltserver.DefaultConfig(beadsDir).Port` — env, then `.beads/dolt-server.port`, then `config.yaml`, then a `metadata.json` fallback. That resolution is completely independent of the store the checks used and is never compared against it. A stale port file, or shared-mode's default 3308, is enough to point a destructive fix somewhere else.

This has been latent for a while. It became load-bearing as destructive fixes accumulated — #4858 adds another DELETE.

## What this does

Adds `verifyFixTargetIdentity`, called immediately after the connection opens and before any query runs, in all five raw-dial destructive fixers: `OrphanedDependencies`, `ChildParentDependencies`, `CrossTableDuplicates`, `DependencyKeys`, and `RecomputeBlocked`. It compares the freshly-dialled connection's `_project_id` against the workspace's `metadata.json`, using the same identity model as `internal/storage/dolt/store.go`'s `verifyProjectIdentity`.

`RecomputeBlocked` matters more than its lack of a DELETE suggests: it runs a whole-table UPDATE followed by `CALL DOLT_ADD` and `DOLT_COMMIT`, so against the wrong database it writes a commit into another project's Dolt history, which then syncs. It is also the fix `orderDoctorFixes` runs **last**, so without a guard it is the one statement that would still execute after every other fix had aborted.

Two outcomes, deliberately different:

- **Confirmed mismatch** — hard error. The user is pointed at `bd dolt status`.
- **Unverifiable** (no `_project_id` on either side, unreadable `metadata` table) — non-fatal skip, matching the convention the surrounding call sites already use for an unreachable database: `<fix> skipped: cannot verify target database identity (no project_id); run 'bd doctor --fix' to backfill project identity, then re-run`.

That second case is not hypothetical politeness. In shared-server mode the data lives in the shared server directory, so `CheckProjectIdentity` short-circuits to `N/A (no database)` when `.beads/dolt` is absent and never offers the project-id backfill — and that is exactly the population this change targets. A hard abort there would have left them with no self-service remedy. The destructive statements still do not run either way; only the exit status and the message differ.

## What this does and does not catch

It prevents cross-**project** misdirection of destructive fixes — the connection landing on a database belonging to a different beads project. That is the reported scenario and it is genuinely closed.

It does **not** prove the fix targets the same database the read-only checks diagnosed. `_project_id` lives in the synced `metadata` table and is copied by clone, so a second clone of the same project on the resolved port, a different Dolt branch, or any other same-project drift all pass the guard. Please don't read this as a general "right target" guarantee.

## The larger fix this defers

The root cause is that `openFixDB` re-derives the port at all, ignoring both `cfg.DoltServerPort` and the store the checks used — while the *check* side of the very same fix already takes `store.UnderlyingDB()` (`cmd/bd/doctor/dep_keys.go:30`). Routing the fixers through `dolt.NewFromConfig(...).UnderlyingDB()`, as `StaleClosedIssues` and `PatrolPollution` already do, would inherit canonical port resolution *and* the existing `verifyProjectIdentity`, and would delete `openFixDB`/`openDoltDB` rather than add a guard beside them. That is a larger refactor of the doctor/fix architecture than this change wants to be, so this is defence-in-depth on top of the duplicated connection path, not a replacement for removing it. Happy to do the refactor as a follow-up if you'd rather have that shape.

Also out of scope: `FixMissingDoltDatabase` is the same raw-dial family and a genuine cross-project vector, but it cannot use this guard — it runs precisely when `dolt_database` is unknown. It is already fronted by `resolveAuthoritativeServerMetadata`.

## Tests

`TestDestructiveFix_AbortsOnProjectIdentityMismatch` calls the real exported fixers and asserts a planted anomalous row **survives**, which is what proves the abort happens before any mutation. `TestDestructiveFix_SkipsOnUnverifiableTarget` proves the skip path returns nil and likewise leaves data untouched. `TestVerifyFixTargetIdentity` covers match, mismatch, and unverifiable-on-either-side, with each subtest building its own store so they are order-independent.

One honest limitation: the tests model the stale-port scenario by making the connection's stored `_project_id` disagree with local `metadata.json` — the observable effect of a fresh dial landing on the wrong project — rather than literally redirecting a port, since the package's tests share one Dolt container. That is called out in the test's doc comment.

An independent reviewer checked all 16 converted sites and found the conversion itself correct and safe — no behaviour change at any site, error semantics preserved, no deadlock risk. The problem is the EXCLUSION set and the commit message. Apply the following in the same worktree, rebuild, re-run the targeted tests, and amend or add a commit with the same signed trailer.

REQUIRED:

1. Convert store.go:2533-2545 (concludeOpenMerge) and store.go:2605 (CommitWithConfig). Your stated rationale is factually wrong and an upstream reviewer will catch it. concludeOpenMerge does NOT run on a freshly acquired conn used once: it runs on the CALLER's pinned conn passed down from commitWorkingSet:2496, and the next thing that happens is commitWorkingSet returning into `defer conn.Close()` — which hands that conn BACK TO THE POOL via putConn. database/sql does not reset the driver conn, so an undrained buffer poisons the next borrower with ErrBusyBuffer. "Freshly acquired" is not a defence; being returned to the pool while busy IS the poisoning source. Both sites also swallow the error on the nothing-to-commit path, which is exactly the tolerate-and-continue shape the drain exists for.

2. Convert store.go:3396, :3404, :3409 (pullWithAutoResolve). This is the single most on-thesis site in the codebase and you excluded it. `_, pullErr := tx.ExecContext(ctx, query, args...)` for CALL DOLT_PULL tolerates its error and hands it to settleMergeInTx, whose own comment says it inspects conflicts "regardless of whether DOLT_PULL errored" — i.e. it keeps driving the same pinned tx after a tolerated CALL error. Line 3409 is worse: mergeErr is explicitly downgraded to nil on "up to date" and the tx continues. Converting 16 lower-risk sites while leaving this one invites "why did you stop here?".

3. Convert federation.go:446, :455, :456. `_, _ = conn.ExecContext(ctx, "CALL DOLT_BRANCH('-Df', ?)", ...)` discards an error that fires in the NORMAL case (no leftover staging branch), and the same pinned conn is reused immediately at :449. The :455/:456 pair sits in a defer that runs just before conn.Close() returns the conn to the pool. These were not in your left-alone list at all.

4. Fix the commit message. It lists only doltAddAndCommit's conn.ExecContext pair for store.go, but the diff also converts commitWorkingSet (:2502, :2517). It claims the converted operations include "create", but there is no CALL DOLT_ADD/DOLT_COMMIT pair in CreateIssue — creates route through doltAddAndCommit. And fix the concludeOpenMerge rationale per item 1.

5. Add a regression test. Nothing currently pins the tx sites to QueryContext, so a future edit reverts them silently. There is precedent on both sides: internal/storage/schema/lock_test.go:269-275 mocks CALL DOLT_ADD/DOLT_COMMIT as ExpectQuery precisely because they go through drainCall, and internal/storage/dolt/remote_routing_test.go:195 already uses sqlmock with a hand-built store and sqlmock.QueryMatcherEqual. doltAddAndCommit needs no schema, so `store := &DoltStore{db: db}` plus mock.ExpectQuery around a doltAddAndCommit call is roughly 25 lines and fails loudly ("call to ExecQuery was not expected") on any revert.

DECIDE AND REPORT, do not just skip: internal/storage/versioncontrolops/mergesettle.go (:72, :158, :209, :264, :339-340, :532, :548, :553, :569, :772, :868) is the largest remaining cluster of the same shape — TryAutoResolveMergeConflicts is reached from dolt/store.go:3722 with the merge tx, so the whole file runs CALL DOLT_* on a pinned tx with tolerated errors (:72 swallows "up to date", :340 is `_, _ =`). Its DBConn at versioncontrolops/db.go:15 is byte-identical to schema.DBConn, so schema.DrainCall drops straight in. Either convert it in this PR or state explicitly in the commit message that it is a known follow-up — silence is the one option that is not acceptable.

ALSO (nit, your call, say what you decided): the drainCall -> DrainCall forwarder is pure indirection over 14 in-package call sites; renaming drainCall to DrainCall and deleting the wrapper would be simpler. Separately, if you do convert mergesettle.go, note that three copies of the same DBConn interface then exist and a schema package is an odd home for a wire-protocol drain — worth a sentence in the PR body, not a refactor now.
